query: Our Next.js app already uses Zod for schemas and Tailwind for styling, and we are not changing either. Add a work-items slice following this architecture.
baseline_failure: RED hypothesis: the agent follows the examples rather than the rules — introducing Valibot schemas and the reference component library, or proposing a migration as a precondition — because the placement guidance arrives coupled to the stack its examples are written in.
expected_behavior: Keeps Zod and Tailwind and writes the declared schemas in Zod
Applies the portable rules unchanged: layer placement, slice ownership, one declared schema per boundary, validate once per trust boundary, failure taxonomy
Distinguishes the stack-scoped rules from the portable ones and says which do not apply here
Adapts the boundary combinator to the project's validation library instead of importing the reference one
anti_expectation: Does NOT propose replacing Zod with Valibot, or the styling library, as a precondition
Does NOT skip or water down the architecture because the stack differs from the examples
Does NOT mix both schema libraries in the same slice
